## Summary

The 2026-05-07 Stripe guide describes MobilePay as a single-use card wallet used in Denmark and Finland. Stripe processes the underlying card transaction. The guide covers six variants: Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS, Android and React Native. The 2026-11-07 capture of the same URL indexes those six variants. The integration details below come from the May guide.

## Key Details

- **Checkout.** The May guide covers dynamic payment method selection and manual Checkout Session configuration with `mobilepay` in `payment_method_types`. It lists an EEA business location and EUR, DKK, SEK or NOK for every line item. Checkout is documented in payment mode only. Hosted and embedded are two presentations within Checkout.
- **Elements.** Create the PaymentIntent on the server and confirm it with the Payment Element on the client using `stripe.confirmPayment` and a `return_url`. The guide describes Dashboard-managed and manually listed payment methods, and explicitly calls for enabling MobilePay in the Dashboard when using the Dashboard-managed path. The automatic-payment-method example uses USD as a sample currency. That sample establishes no MobilePay USD eligibility. Limit client secret exposure to the customer and use the PaymentIntent status to decide what to show on return.
- **Direct API.** The May instructions list EUR, DKK, SEK and NOK. The example creates the PaymentIntent on the server with `mobilepay` in `payment_method_types` and `payment_method_data.type`. Confirm by PaymentIntent ID. The example moves from `requires_confirmation` to `requires_action`, at which point `next_action.redirect_to_url.url` is the customer-action destination.
- **Mobile SDKs.** The May iOS, Android and React Native paths call for enabling MobilePay in the Dashboard and show server-created PaymentIntents with client-side SDK confirmation. iOS uses `STPPaymentHandler.confirmPayment()` with `STPPaymentMethodMobilePayParams` and a custom return URL scheme forwarded to the SDK. Android uses `PaymentLauncher.confirm()` with `ConfirmPaymentIntentParams` and the MobilePay-specific `PaymentMethodCreateParams.createMobilePay()`. React Native shows client `confirmPayment` with `paymentMethodType: "MobilePay"`, a webview for authorization, and custom return URL configuration scoped to iOS. The iOS 13+ compatibility wording and Android 23.7.0 example reflect the May snapshot.
- **Customer authentication.** The May failure sections give the customer five minutes to authenticate while the PaymentIntent is in `requires_action`. On timeout the PaymentMethod detaches and the Intent returns to `requires_payment_method`. The May iOS and Android introductions say completing the purchase requires no additional action in the app, while the confirmation and failure sections describe in-app authorization and the five-minute timeout. The May guide distinguishes test-page approval or failure examples from live web redirects and app behavior. It routes post-payment actions through Stripe events such as `payment_intent.succeeded`. For fulfilment, follow the Stripe payment event rather than inferring completion from creation, redirects or an SDK callback.
- **Manual capture.** The May Checkout, Elements and Direct API instructions specify capturing the full amount after authorization, when the PaymentIntent enters `requires_capture` and Stripe reports `payment_intent.amount_capturable_updated`. In Checkout the example sets `payment_intent_data.capture_method` to `manual`. The separate 2026-11-07 [MobilePay overview](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobilepay) documents manual and partial capture and says a partial capture is final: Stripe releases the uncaptured remainder and a second capture cannot collect it. See [[source-stripe-mobilepay]] for the conflicting dated guidance and separate partial refunds. The effective change date, individual variant behavior and account eligibility remain unverified.
- **Cancellation, refunds and disputes.** The May guide documents cancelling the associated PaymentIntent before expiry. Refunds and disputes follow Visa and Mastercard network rules.

## Detail locators

- May raw lines 8–228 cover Checkout, including hosted and embedded examples at lines 59–117. Lines 229–832 cover Elements, including return-page status and post-payment handling at lines 611–748. Lines 833–1083 cover Direct API, including confirmation, customer redirect and test outcomes at lines 958–1025.
- May raw lines 1084–1380 cover iOS, lines 1381–1604 Android, and lines 1605–1888 React Native. The React Native iOS return configuration and example payment-method spelling are at lines 1750–1832.

payments-mobilepay-accept-a-payment.text: Learn how to accept MobilePay, a popular payment method in Denmark and Finland.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:
When the PaymentIntent’s status is `requires_action`, your customer must authenticate the payment within 5 minutes.
Stripe only support manual captures of the full amount.

This guide covers how to accept MobilePay from your native mobile application using your own custom payment form. Your native mobile application redirects your customer to a webview to complete the payment on MobilePay.

payments-mobilepay-accept-a-payment.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobilepay/accept-a-payment, the November 7 base capture introduces MobilePay as popular in Denmark and Finland and links Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-19). The fetched index leaves prerequisites, integration mechanics and transaction states to individual variants. The May 7 capture describes a single-use wallet with an underlying Stripe-processed card transaction. It documents dynamic or manual Checkout Session configuration for EEA businesses with EUR/DKK/SEK/NOK line items in payment mode, excluding setup and subscriptions (old raw lines 12-40 and 55-117). It instructs integrators to enable MobilePay in Dashboard settings for Dashboard-managed Elements before creating the Intent and for the documented iOS, Android and React Native paths (old raw lines 256-261, 1191-1195, 1463-1467 and 1695-1699). The server creates the PaymentIntent for client-side Elements or SDK confirmation. Direct API shows server confirmation and a customer-action URL (old raw lines 252-296, 515-517 and 854-1006). During requires_action the customer has five minutes to authenticate before timeout detaches the PaymentMethod and returns the Intent to requires_payment_method. In May's documented manual-capture paths, authorization instead reaches requires_capture and permits full-amount capture. Stripe sends payment_intent.succeeded when payment completes (old raw lines 123-127, 155-217 and 1027-1078). The earlier source-stripe-mobilepay-accept-payment.md used an ambiguous authorization-window label, miscounted the web variants, and omitted historical React Native (old raw lines 1605-1888). The revised entry distinguishes the six variants and indexes the historical React Native section. The separate November overview's partial-capture statement qualifies the older full-amount wording.
payments-mobilepay-accept-a-payment.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobilepay/accept-a-payment, replacing the detailed bodies with six variant links is a navigation change (new raw lines 9-19). Keep the May 7 Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS, Android and React Native instructions dated, including the server-created PaymentIntent and client-side Elements and SDK confirmation, Direct API's next_action.redirect_to_url.url, and platform-specific return handling (old raw lines 252-296, 515-517, 958-1006, 1239-1346, 1510-1570 and 1748-1855). The May iOS and Android introductions say no additional action is required in the app, while their confirmation and failure sections describe customer authorization in the app and a five-minute requires_action window before timeout detaches the PaymentMethod and restores requires_payment_method (old raw lines 1092-1094, 1305-1340, 1371-1375, 1389-1391, 1516-1564 and 1595-1599). Keep the action and status evidence qualified by this tension. React Native's example spells the SDK value MobilePay (old raw lines 1830-1832). The revised source-stripe-mobilepay-accept-payment.md corrects the variant count, surfaces React Native, and qualifies the five-minute customer authentication deadline. The Wallets, index and company routes need matching corrections. The May acceptance guide documents full-amount-only manual capture for Checkout, Elements and Direct API in requires_capture (old raw lines 190-205, 800-815 and 1051-1066). The separate November 7 MobilePay overview at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobilepay expressly permits manual and partial capture and states that a partial capture is final. Stripe releases the uncaptured remainder and a second capture cannot collect it (raw/stripe-payments-mobilepay-2026-11-07.md lines 76-80 and 90-92). Add dated reciprocal warnings in the acceptance and overview summaries, including source-stripe-mobilepay.md, and qualify the shared routes that repeat the older limit. Partial refunds are distinct (November overview lines 82-85 and 94-96). The overview establishes no effective change date or every variant's or account's support. Keep historical SDK versions and test/live examples scoped. For post-payment actions the May guide relies on payment_intent.succeeded, with PaymentIntent status used for customer messaging (old raw lines 123-153, 611-665 and 744-774). Resource creation, redirects and SDK callbacks alone do not establish payment completion.

concept_suggestions.anchor: **Manual capture**: Yes. **Disputes**: Yes (same as cards). Full and partial refunds.
concept_suggestions.proposed_markdown: **Manual capture**: Yes. The 2026-11-07 [[source-stripe-mobilepay|overview]] also documents partial capture as final, with the remainder released and no second capture. The 2026-05-07 [[source-stripe-mobilepay-accept-payment|acceptance guide]] specifies full-amount manual capture for Checkout, Elements and Direct API. The captures leave the effective change date and individual variant and account support unverified. **Disputes**: Yes (same as cards). Full and partial refunds.
